method: Sources fetched 2026-10-30 via WebFetch, curl (arXiv, Europe PMC full-text XML, Copernicus GMD PDFs, White Rose and HAL accepted manuscripts, author/third-party PDF mirrors) and pdftotext; abstracts from Crossref and Semantic Scholar APIs. DOIs checked against Crossref titles. Nominal rows record one stated size per row; effective rows only where a source states a number for a stated region, variable, period and estimator. Quotes from PDF text extraction were normalized for ligatures and math glyphs (pdftotext renders approximately-equal as 'ø' and '=' as '5' in the 1999 J. Climate scans). Quotes returned through WebFetch were extracted by the fetch tool's summarizer from the fetched page; they are marked checked_in_text true but are one step removed from raw text.

rows.item: ERA5 HRES atmosphere

rows.item: FORESEE-urban dark-fiber DAS (Pennsylvania) and Brady Hot Springs DAS
rows.quantity: low-rank SVD compression behaviour (no rank or variance fraction stated)
rows.method: SVD rank / compression ratio (randomized truncated SVD of channel x time matrices)
rows.value_text: SVD compression tested at 5x to 100x; detection significance of mid-sized and large events preserved at 100x; error growth explained by a close to uniform distribution of singular values
rows.source: Issah & Martin (n.d., CWP-1027), Center for Wave Phenomena Report, Colorado School of Mines
rows.quote: the steady rate of growth in errors may be explained by a close to uniform distribution of singular values of the seismic data used
rows.notes: The only DAS low-rank result found. It argues against a sharply low-rank DAS record: singular values decay slowly, so the 100x figure is a lossy-compression tolerance for event detection, not an intrinsic dimension. No rank r or variance fraction is reported. FORESEE window: 10 days, 2019-04-09 to 2019-04-21; Brady: 2016 microseismicity.

rows.item: Wolf Volcano (Galapagos) 2015 eruption, 20 daisy-chain descending Sentinel-1 interferograms, 2014-12-13 to 2015-10-21, coherence < 0.8 masked
rows.quantity: number of independent components retained / recovered
rows.method: PCA whitening then spatial ICA (FastICA)
rows.value_text: six components recovered from 20 interferograms; components 1, 2 and 6 interpreted as deformation (three signals), the rest atmospheric; PCs 6-20 judged turbulent atmosphere
rows.source: Gaddes et al. (2018), Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
rows.quote: As around 3–4 geophysical signals are expected, we set the FastICA algorithm to recover six components
rows.notes: The 6 is a user choice informed by expected sources and inspection of PCs, not a variance threshold. Abstract: 'automatically isolate three signals'. Nominal dimension of the stack is 20 interferograms.

rows.item: Calbuco (Chile) 2015 eruption, ~50 x 50 km subset of Sentinel-1A track 164 daisy-chain interferograms
rows.quantity: dimension retained after PCA whitening before ICA
rows.method: PCA whitening then spatial and temporal ICA (FastICA)
rows.value_text: Twelve interferograms ... data dimensions were reduced to ten
rows.source: Ebmeier (2016), Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
rows.quote: Twelve interferograms (Supplementary Table 1) were used in the analysis and the data dimensions were reduced to ten during preparation and whitening.
rows.notes: Accepted manuscript read. Retained dimension chosen by trial and error (author's stated approach), not a variance criterion; one IC cluster captured co-eruptive deformation. Shows that with tens of interferograms the retained dimension is bounded by the number of epochs.

rows.item: Northern Hemisphere wintertime 500-mb height pentads, DJF 1946-93 (48 winters), NMC analyses, 5 x 7.5 degree grid north of 20N, 672 grid points, anomalies, area-weighted
rows.quantity: effective number of spatial degrees of freedom, eigenvalue formula
rows.method: effective spatial degrees of freedom N*_ef (Bretherton et al. 1999 eigenvalue formula)
rows.value_text: N*ef ≈ 19 (fitted 18.5); first N*ef EOFs explain about 82% of the variance
rows.source: Bretherton et al. (1999), Journal of Climate
rows.quote: χ2 distributions with N*mm = 23.8 (solid) and N*ef = 18.5 (dashed) degrees of freedom
rows.notes: Read from a third-party mirror of the AMS PDF. Nominal dimension 672 grid points vs effective ~19. Wallace et al. (1991) found 20 DOF best fit the same data. Insensitive to grid spacing up to 1500 km per the paper. Quote is the Figure 4 caption.

rows.item: Same NH DJF 500-mb pentad data set as dim-26 (672 grid points, 1946-93)
rows.quantity: effective number of spatial degrees of freedom, moment-matching estimate
rows.method: effective spatial degrees of freedom N*_mm (moment matching of chi-square)
rows.value_text: N*mm ≈ 24 (fitted 23.8)
rows.source: Bretherton et al. (1999), Journal of Climate
rows.quote: We see that in this dataset, for large sample sizes, N*mm ≈ 24 is indeed systematically larger than N*ef ≈ 19
rows.notes: Two estimators on the same field differ by ~25%; the paper argues N*mm suits variance tests and N*ef suits covariance/correlation tests.

rows.item: Same NH DJF 500-mb pentad data set as dim-26
rows.quantity: number of EOFs needed to explain 90% of variance
rows.method: PCA/EOF variance captured
rows.value_text: leading 10 modes explain only about 68%; 27 modes required to explain 90%
rows.source: Bretherton et al. (1999), Journal of Climate
rows.quote: the leading 10 modes explain only about 68% of the overall variance and 27 modes are required to explain 90%
rows.notes: Same field gives 19, 24 or 27 depending on estimator and threshold.

rows.item: Daily precipitation at 113 Swiss rain gauges, winters DJF 1961-90
rows.quantity: effective number of spatial degrees of freedom
rows.method: effective spatial degrees of freedom N*_ef (eigenvalue formula); N*_mm also reported
rows.value_text: N*mm = 0.24 and N*ef = 2.4; 80% of variance in three leading EOFs; monthly totals give N*mm 0.9, N*ef 1.7

rows.quote: Over the entire data record, the two estimators of ESDOF are N*mm = 0.24 and N*ef = 2.4.
rows.notes: N*mm < 1 because of heavy-tailed PCs; authors say it is not literally a number of degrees of freedom. Nominal dimension 113 gauges.
